title: Four nations back Pakistan's Iran-US peace effort
credits: Photos: Cengiz Özarpat, Popup Agency / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Four Muslim powers have publicly backed Pakistan's peace effort between Iran and the United States.
At a meeting in Istanbul on Friday, the R4 group, Pakistan, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Egypt, issued a joint statement.
It expressed support for the Islamabad MoU, the Pakistan-brokered understanding meant to keep the pause in US-Iran hostilities from collapsing.
The ministers said the conflict with Iran must be addressed only through dialogue and diplomacy.
They called for the swift and full resumption of safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz.
They strongly condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, and on shipping in the Red Sea.
On Palestine, they backed an independent state on the nineteen sixty-seven lines, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
Then, for the first time, they sat down with Britain, France and Germany, joined by Italy.
Türkiye's foreign minister, Hakan Fidan, said military intervention in Iran is by no means a solution.
France's foreign minister said the eight countries agreed to keep meeting at regular intervals.
For Pakistan, it is a diplomatic boost for its role as a mediator between Washington and Tehran.
